judgement.voice: Tie on the best twelve. Covered, Maximilian's best lines are his: no contractions, 'Do' and 'shall' imperatives, and a hotel object as the turn (carriage, carpet, coats, trouser press). But part of that identity is topic (hotel nouns), not sentence shape, and Vera has a shape that survives any topic: the repeat-then-turn fake-out (#12) and the rhetorical tag that assumes your complicity ('Right?', #47; 'Right. Now.', #48). Taken across the whole bank Maximilian loses voice badly (see genericLines); on the best twelve it holds.
judgement.construction: Ours, narrowly. Maximilian's best twelve are tighter than Vera's set: turn on the last two to five words, no explanation, nothing after the punch ('And its parents.', 'I had it built in your century.'). Vera's #49 and #51 are baggy and lean on the setup. Credit where due.
judgement.quotable: Bar. Vera's lines carry stakes: she assumes you will cover up a murder, drinks the tears of her enemies, and the narrator treats her empathy as a weather event. Those are clipped and shared. Maximilian's best are drawing-room clever and never dangerous; nobody clips 'You are creasing the carpet'. His jokes rate the suitor; they never reveal anything outrageous that Maximilian takes for granted about himself, which is where Vera's status comedy lives.
judgement.verdict: If both sets ran tonight, Vera is the better written character. Maximilian is the better constructed one line by line, but he has no outrageous presumption and no visible secret Y (Vera: mean, and empathy is an anomaly), so he reads as a witty maitre d', not a character.

templates: A. Echo the suitor's gimmick back at them (dashboard, funnel, ticket, hold music, junk folder, fee, unsubscribe, recalculate, rep, recall notice, Variant B): about 60 lines across react, cut, oneOnOne and pick. The suitor's vocabulary does the joke, Maximilian only adds 'Mr' or 'Madam', which is why Vesper and Pixel have the same lines.

B. Cash the suitor's CAST.md secret (how was your day, finish the poem, I am replying, on purpose, sit still, the door and the cheese, first conversion, you did well): 28 of the 32 oneOnOne and pick lines. All three star banks mined the same column and landed on the same eight beats, two of them near verbatim.

C. 'Lovely X.' faint praise then the but (Lovely. Now say..., Lovely. Is there a version..., Lovely offer, Lovely voice, Lovely energy, Lovely words, your metrics are lovely, No hedging. Lovely.): 8 lines.

D. 'Please stop X. I am not a Y.' / 'Please do not X' (funnel, rep, accounts, grovelling, narrate the menu, faint on the marble, two a.m. habits, no verse before dessert, my file is not open): about 12 lines.

E. Staccato verdict 'Adjective. Adjective. Short sentence.' (Ridiculous. Gorgeous. / Absurd. Generous. / Vicious. Specific. / Short. Clean. / Too much. Far too much. / Ouch. Accurate. / Calm, direct and on time. / Correct. Also beautifully pressed. / Humble. And so accurate): 9 lines. Two of these are best lines; nine is a tic.

F. Statement, then a one-word deflating adverb (Briefly. Eventually. Probably. Mostly. Strictly. Kindly. Sharp. Slowly. Slowly. Slower.): about 10 lines. 'Slowly' or 'slower' alone appears four times.
G. The car as the exit (three cars, collected, Shall I call you a car, car park twice, cancel your car, car already running, carriage): 8 lines. The persona prescribes it; the bank spends it.

H. Bare-adjective appetite 'I adore X / I have missed X / I hate that X' (I adore specific, I adore dry, I adore a guest with a file, I have missed accurate, I hate that it worked, I hate that she is right): 6 lines.

You taught me that." / "Mr Brock, wonderful effort. Please cool down in the car park." / "Oh, she is good. I am almost rattled."
Stock romance filler by another name: "Vex. You knew. Of course you knew. Come here anyway."
Real brand by echo: "Sir, this is a dinner, not a quarterly review." is the 'Sir, this is a Wendy's' meme frame.
Voice slip: the only contraction in a bank that otherwise never contracts, "That was real, wasn't it. Give me a moment." (also "The other's car is already running.", which is a possessive and fine).
biggestGap: Maximilian's turn is borrowed: in most reacts, every cut, one-on-one and pick, the punchline is the suitor's own gimmick or CAST.md secret with 'Mr' in front, so his lines are near copies of Vesper's and Pixel's, and his own persona device, warmth as 'an upgrade you did not authorise', appears in none of the 16 picks. In the next pass, make the turn of every line a hotel procedure that shows what he takes for granted (he owns the building; suitors are guests he can upgrade, bill, relocate, comp, blacklist or have collected), with the suitor's gimmick only as the setup, and rebuild the picks and one-on-ones around keys, rooms, late checkout and upgrades he pretends not to have signed.

notes: Bar file present (monster-prom-lines.md, wiki-sourced) and read in full, including the voice section; charm-notes.md read. I also read vesper.json and pixel.json to test 'another member of our cast could have said it', and the overlap is the main finding: the one-on-one, pick and cut sections of all three star banks share the same eight beats, mined from CAST.md's secret column (Frost's 'opening the door, and not for cheese' appears in all three). Generic share is 92 of 191 lines (48%), every one listed verbatim in genericLines with its reason: mostly cross-cast or 'anyone' lines, then stock lines, self-explaining lines and template members beyond one exemplar. Count: intro 4, questions 12, react 48, cardReact 48, cut 16, twistIntro 12, ex 3, oneOnOne 16, hold 4, pick 16, reveal 9, outro 3. The strongest sections are cardReact (where his own hotel logic does the turn: 'We do not discuss the rate in the lobby.', 'Honesty belongs on the comment card. Not at dinner.', 'Fears go in the safe, not on the table.', 'Policy, recited. How very night shift.', 'That is how the pool got closed. No.'), the ex lines, and the reveal 'none' set. Also worth protecting just outside the top five: 'That sentence arrived with luggage. I am still unpacking.', 'You asked about me. Somebody cancel your car.', 'Absurd. Generous. I am reaching for a pen. Stop me.', 'Oh dear. Sincere. We have no policy for sincere.', 'Unprompted contrition. You were raised in a good hotel.', 'Turn-on: {card}. Whoever found it may keep the robe.', '{card}. Untouched all night, like the trouser press.', 'Thank you for shopping with us. He never thanked me. He tipped me. Which is worse.', 'Two guests. One suite. Housekeeping, stand by.' Secondary gap against Vera: Maximilian has no X-but-secretly-Y. Monster Prom builds every character as a contradiction the lines keep exposing; the self-checkout ex is the only crack in him, and the bank never lets it leak into the show (for example, a concierge who has never once been a guest).
